title: Case split on Nontrivial G and p divides |G| for Dickson's classification of finite PGL2 subgroups
intent: Reduce Dickson's classification of the finite subgroups of PGL2(Fbar_p) — an 8-way disjunction — to two named lemmas, one per side of a `p divides |G|` split, plus a trivial subsingleton case, each re-indexed into the goal by a chain of `Or.inl`/`Or.inr`.

parent.name: Dickson.dickson_classification
parent.statement:
theorem dickson_classification (G : Subgroup (PGLOf (K p))) [Finite G] :
    (IsCyclic G) ∨
    (∃ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* DihedralGroup n)) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 4))) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin 4))) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 5))) ∨
    (∃ (m t : ℕ) (_ : m ≥ 1) (_ : Nat.Coprime t p) (_ : t ∣ p ^ m - 1)
      (φ : Multiplicative (ZMod t) →* MulAut (Multiplicative (Fin m → ZMod p))),
      Nonempty (G ≃* (Multiplicative (Fin m → ZMod p)) ⋊[φ] Multiplicative (ZMod t))) ∨
    (∃ m : ℕ, m ≥ 1 ∧
      Nonempty (G ≃* Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m))) ∨
    (∃ m : ℕ, m ≥ 1 ∧
      Nonempty (G ≃* (GL (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m) ⧸
        Subgroup.center (GL (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m)))))

children.name: Dickson.classification_wild_slop
children.statement:
theorem classification_wild_slop (G : Subgroup (PGLOf (K p))) [Finite G]
    (hG_p : p ∣ Nat.card G) :
    (∃ (m t : ℕ) (_ : m ≥ 1) (_ : Nat.Coprime t p) (_ : t ∣ p ^ m - 1)
      (φ : Multiplicative (ZMod t) →* MulAut (Multiplicative (Fin m → ZMod p))),
      Nonempty (G ≃* (Multiplicative (Fin m → ZMod p)) ⋊[φ] Multiplicative (ZMod t))) ∨
    (∃ m : ℕ, m ≥ 1 ∧
      Nonempty (G ≃* Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m))) ∨
    (∃ m : ℕ, m ≥ 1 ∧
      Nonempty (G ≃* (GL (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m) ⧸
        Subgroup.center (GL (Fin 2) (GaloisField p m))))) ∨
    (p = 3 ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 5)))

children.name: Dickson.classification_tame_slop
children.statement:
theorem classification_tame_slop (G : Subgroup (PGLOf (K p))) [Fintype G]
    (hG_tame : ¬ (p : ℕ) ∣ Nat.card G)
    (hG_nontrivial : Nontrivial G) :
    (IsCyclic G) ∨
    (∃ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* DihedralGroup n)) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 4))) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin 4))) ∨
    (Nonempty (G ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 5)))

applicability.goal_shape: A goal that is a finite disjunction (here an 8-way `∨` of mutually exclusive group-isomorphism cases) over a quantified object `G`, where the truth of the disjuncts is controlled by a small set of decidable hypotheses on `G` (nontriviality; divisibility of the order by a fixed prime).
applicability.use_when: the target is a classification theorem whose cases are indexed by a few decidable predicates, and one named lemma already exists for each branch; the glue is then only `by_cases` + `rcases` + re-indexing `Or.inl`/`Or.inr`.
applicability.avoid_when: the cases overlap or are not a partition, so the disjunction needs a canonical representative; the per-branch lemmas do not already exist (then the split is not the content, the branch lemmas are); or the re-indexing would be into a deep, shifting disjunction where a `match`/`induction` on a dedicated `cases`-type is clearer.

claims.claim: The parent's proof closes from exactly two project lemmas plus mathlib facts: the `Nontrivial G` branch splits again on `p ∣ Nat.card G`, the `p ∣` case is closed by `classification_wild_slop` (line 70), the `¬ p ∣` case by `classification_tame_slop` (line 76), and the subsingleton case by `not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton` and `Subgroup.mem_zpowers` (lines 82-83).

No branch is closed by a hole: the files holding the parent and its two children (DicksonClassification.lean, WildClassification.lean, TameClassification.lean, and the tame leaves' file CyclicPartition.lean) contain no `sorry`, `admit`, or `axiom`.

consequences: The two `by_cases` create three branches (trivial / wild / tame) whose exhaustiveness is automatic (each is `Classical.em` on a decidable predicate), so unlike a residue split there is no separate exhaustiveness child. The cost is the re-indexing: each child proves a disjunction with a different number and order of disjuncts than the parent (wild is a 4-way disjunction, tame a 5-way, parent an 8-way), so every branch must be re-targeted by a chain of `Or.inl`/`Or.inr`; the `p = 3` exceptional case of the wild side lands on the same `alternatingGroup (Fin 5)` disjunct as the tame side, and a wrong re-index would silently misplace it. Failure mode: if the parent's disjunction order changes, every `Or.inr <| Or.inr <| …` chain silently points at the wrong disjunct (they are positional, not by name).
